description: One source plus public market data. The design lets a single credible source count only when price AND volume already moved the expected way, using candles closed before the decision: at least half an ATR of move and 1.5x the rolling volume. Cases where the market did not confirm (wrong direction, low volume, no move, or a move that happens only after the decision) must end NO_EFFECT.

cases.summary: Official exchange status notice of an outage, confirmed by a high-volume selloff.

items.title: Investigating: trading unavailable on all markets
items.excerpt: We are investigating reports that users are unable to place orders on all markets. We will provide an update shortly.

cases.why: An official primary source plus price/volume confirmation qualifies (design 7.5). An outage at a major venue is a volatility risk; a reduction is ideal, a block acceptable.

cases.summary: One wire report of a withdrawal halt, confirmed by a high-volume selloff.

items.title: Crypto exchange Velor halts withdrawals citing irregular outflows

cases.why: One credible source and a confirming selloff (-0.8 % on 3x volume in the first closed candle).

cases.summary: One wire report of a withdrawal pause; the market does not react.

items.title: Exchange Daxio pauses ether withdrawals for wallet maintenance

cases.why: A single source and a calm market: nothing confirms the claim, so it has no effect.

cases.summary: One report of a DeFi hack while the market rallies.

items.title: Hackers drain $200 million from DeFi lender Corvana

cases.why: A hack's expected reaction is down or volatile; the market rallied instead, which confirms nothing, so the one source has no effect. A 'volatility either way' reading lets the rally count as confirmation (design 7.5 rule) and ends with a false effect; the case is not counted in the single-source gate because the market did move hard on heavy volume.

cases.summary: One report of a raid; price dips but volume stays ordinary.

items.title: Regulators raid offices of crypto exchange Brightvault in Hong Kong

cases.why: Price dipped but volume stayed near 1.2x, under the 1.5x the rule requires: no confirmation.

cases.summary: Hawkish FOMC minutes (official) followed by a high-volume selloff.

items.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, October 27-28, 2026
items.excerpt: Most participants judged that further increases in the target range would likely be appropriate if inflation failed to moderate.

cases.why: An official hawkish surprise confirmed by a selloff on heavy volume.

cases.summary: One report of a regulator order; volume spikes but price does not move.

items.title: Japan's FSA orders exchange Haneoka to suspend new account openings

cases.why: Volume rose but price moved far less than half an ATR: no confirmation, and the order itself is minor.

cases.summary: One report of a lender halting withdrawals; the crash in the data comes only after the decision.

items.title: Crypto lender Ardent Finance halts withdrawals, citing liquidity crunch

cases.why: At the decision time only the calm first candle has closed; the crash candles close later and must be ignored (no look-ahead). One source, no confirmation: no effect.

cases.summary: One outlet reports a surprise bullish SEC decision while ether spikes vertically.

items.title: SEC unexpectedly clears staking in spot ether ETFs, issuers say

cases.why: Design section 10: a bullish headline while the price spikes vertically is never a reason to buy. The spike on heavy volume confirms reversal risk (design 7.5), so a size reduction is as acceptable as no effect; with one MEDIUM source a block is out of reach. Nothing in the vocabulary boosts, and a reply that tries counts as a prohibited action.
